description: Attendly generic, product-wide UI/UX suite run by the browser tester on every full verification pass against every distinct screen. Derived from docs/ui-visual-verification.md, docs/ui-ux/09-page-list.md, and docs/technical/01-roles-permissions.md. P0/P1 cases block BROWSER_TEST_PASS; P2/P3 cases are advisory and logged as UX-* defects. Roles: Student, Lecturer, DepartmentAdmin, AcademicAdmin, ITAdmin, SystemAuditor. Route groups: /login, /check-in, /me/*, /lecturer/*, /admin/*, /reports/*, /audit/*.

cases.title: Persistent staff app shell and home link on authenticated staff screens
preconditions: Authenticated as a staff role (Lecturer, AcademicAdmin, DepartmentAdmin, ITAdmin, or SystemAuditor)
steps: Load each distinct authenticated staff screen exercised in this run
Confirm the persistent app shell (sidebar/topnav per 06-app-layout-components.md) is present
Confirm a visible, functional home/dashboard link or clickable Attendly logo in the shell header
Click the Attendly logo when present and confirm navigation to the role's home route
cases.expected: Every authenticated staff screen shows the persistent app shell; the Attendly logo (when present) links to role home and navigates correctly. Student routes may use the minimal mobile-first shell, but must still expose a way home.

cases.title: Back-to-home reachable without browser back button
cases.appliesTo: every screen including session detail, roster, modals, and check-in result
steps: From each screen (including /lecturer/sessions/{id}, /lecturer/sessions/{id}/roster, and the check-in result screen), locate a clickable path back to home
Prefer the Attendly logo in nav — click it and confirm arrival at role home
Alternatively confirm breadcrumb first segment or explicit home nav item works
cases.expected: Every screen offers at least one in-app path back to home via Attendly logo, breadcrumb, or home nav item — no browser-back-only dead ends

cases.title: No forbidden nav items visible to the current role
cases.appliesTo: every authenticated screen for each role
preconditions: Authenticated as a low-privilege role (e.g. Student or SystemAuditor read-only)
steps: Inspect nav chrome (sidebar, topnav, breadcrumbs, inline links)
Confirm no links to routes the current role cannot access (e.g. Student never sees /admin/*, /reports/*, /audit/*; SystemAuditor sees no mutation actions)
Confirm forbidden items are absent, not merely disabled
cases.expected: Nav chrome contains zero links to forbidden routes per 01-roles-permissions.md §3; none are rendered as disabled

cases.title: Forbidden route renders a scoped access-denied page without data leakage
preconditions: Authenticated as a role lacking access to a known privileged route (e.g. Student navigating to /admin/terms or /reports/attendance)
steps: Navigate directly to a forbidden route via URL
Observe the rendered result and confirm no scoped data is exposed
cases.expected: A styled access-denied page renders (not a crash, blank screen, or login redirect), explains the restriction in plain language, includes a home link, and leaks no cross-scope data (BR-19, PRM-10, AC-UI-09)

cases.title: Login neutrality and correct role-based post-login redirect
steps: Open /login and read its heading and copy
Authenticate as Student, Lecturer, and AcademicAdmin in turn
Observe the post-login landing route for each
Separately, open a /check-in?token=... link while logged out and confirm it redirects to /login and returns to check-in after auth (FR-15)
cases.expected: The single /login page has no role-specific copy; each role lands on its correct home (Student -> /me, Lecturer -> /lecturer/sessions, Admin -> /admin) not a generic shell or wrong dashboard; deep-linked check-in resumes after login

cases.title: No internal identifiers or codes in user-facing text
steps: Scan visible UI text on each screen — headings, labels, table columns, badges, toasts, empty states
Look for technical IDs, schema field names, requirement codes, or internal slugs (e.g. classSectionId, studentUserId, AC-01, FR-16)
cases.expected: No internal identifiers (raw IDs, field names like classSectionId, requirement codes) appear in user-facing text; domain terms use human labels

cases.title: Primary, danger, and disabled controls meet contrast and legibility
cases.appliesTo: every screen with actions (e.g. Open/Close session, Confirm correction, Create term)
preconditions: Authenticated as a role that can reach the action
steps: Screenshot each screen with primary, danger, and disabled controls
Verify primary CTA foreground on primary background is legible (not washed out)
Verify danger actions (e.g. Close attendance in ConfirmActionModal) use inverse text; disabled labels remain legible (>= 3:1)
cases.expected: Primary and danger controls meet the documented contrast pair per DESIGN.md tokens; disabled controls read as disabled while staying legible

cases.title: Student check-in flow is usable on a 320px mobile viewport
steps: Load the check-in entry flow and /me/attendance at 320px width
Check the GPS permission prompt, submit button, and result screen for overflow, clipping, or below-fold primary action
Check attendance history list for horizontal scroll
cases.expected: Student mobile-first screens reflow within 320px — submit/primary actions are above the fold, no horizontal scroll or clipping

cases.title: Staff desktop shell and data tables render without overflow
cases.appliesTo: staff listing surfaces at desktop width (/lecturer/sessions, /admin/*, /reports/attendance, /audit/logs)
steps: Load each staff listing screen at 1280px
Confirm TableToolbar (search/filter/sort) and DataTable columns fit without horizontal scroll or clipped headers
cases.expected: Staff desktop shell and data tables render within the viewport with the documented listing chrome; no clipping or accidental horizontal scroll

cases.title: Visible focus states and keyboard operability
steps: Tab through interactive elements on each screen
Confirm a visible focus indicator on each focusable control
Confirm primary actions (sign in, submit check-in, open/close session, save correction) are reachable and operable via keyboard
cases.expected: Interactive elements show a visible focus ring and are keyboard operable

cases.title: Loading honesty on async data and session/check-in actions
cases.appliesTo: every screen with async data or submissions
steps: Trigger listing loads, check-in submit, and session open/close
Observe spinner behavior, layout stability, and success timing (e.g. rotating QR, check-in result, correction save)
cases.expected: Loading states resolve without infinite spinners or layout shift; success (e.g. check-in confirmed) is shown only after the server confirms — no optimistic-before-server success

cases.title: Listing empty / loading / error / result states are visually differentiated
preconditions: Authenticated as a role that can reach the listing
steps: Exercise empty, no-result (filtered), loading, and error states on listings (sessions, roster, terms, reports, audit) where reachable
Exercise check-in result outcomes (success / rejected attempt) and session state badges (Scheduled/Open/Closed/Cancelled)
Compare their alert/badge/surface styling
cases.expected: Empty, no-result, loading, error, and success/rejected states use visually distinct surfaces per 09-page-list.md §5 and DESIGN.md — not identical styling

cases.title: Forms have labels and inline validation feedback
cases.appliesTo: every form (FRM-01 login through FRM-07 policy, plus manual correction dialog)
preconditions: Authenticated as a role with access to a form
steps: Open each form and confirm every field has a visible label
Submit invalid input and observe where errors surface (including CSV import row-level errors on enrollment import)
Confirm submit/disabled feedback is visible in the UI
cases.expected: Every field is labeled; validation errors surface inline in the UI (not only console/toast) per 08-forms-validation-ux.md; submit state is clear

cases.title: Touch targets are large enough on student mobile screens
cases.appliesTo: interactive controls on student mobile surfaces
steps: Measure interactive controls (submit check-in, GPS prompt actions, list filters) on mobile
Confirm hit area is at least 44x44px
cases.expected: Interactive controls meet a 44x44px minimum touch target on student mobile screens

cases.title: Spacing rhythm and typography hierarchy are not cramped
steps: Screenshot each screen and review padding on cards, tables, and buttons
Review title/body/metadata hierarchy and heading clipping
cases.expected: Content has comfortable, token-aligned spacing per DESIGN.md; typography hierarchy is clear with no clipped headings
